title: Multi-language client contract for windowed streaming, backpressure, and graceful fallback
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem statement: SDK teams (Python/TypeScript/Go) need a single, well-scoped contract for streaming APIs that balances developer ergonomics, production reliability, and cross-language compatibility. Current ad-hoc streaming prototypes diverge across languages (frame formats, resume semantics, retry behavior) and risk fragmentation for customer integrations. This ticket defines the product requirements, acceptance criteria, and rollout plan for a unified client contract covering: windowed streaming (client-controlled read windows), backpressure signaling, resume semantics for interrupted streams, retry/idempotency interactions, and graceful fallback to non-streamed responses. The goal is to produce a PRD and acceptance checklist the SDK teams can implement in parallel while preserving runtime flexibility for optimizations.
background_and_context: Users embed LLM-powered streaming in chat UIs, real-time assistants, and transcription flows. There are three recurring operational risks: (1) client libraries handle transient network errors inconsistently, leading to duplicate/incomplete outputs; (2) mobile and browser clients need deterministic backpressure so they can control memory; (3) server-side runtime rollouts require compatible downgrade/fallback behavior so customers do not see broken streams during progressive model swaps. Past PRs: GH-rt/streaming-proto-draft (prototype), design doc in Confluence titled 'Streaming surface v0' (link below). This ticket consolidates those learnings into a product-grade contract.
decision_log: 2026-02-12: Align on two streaming modes: 'delta-chunk' (byte/utf-8 deltas suitable for simple text joins) and 'event-frame' (typed frames with metadata, recommended for structured outputs)
2026-02-16: Adopt opaque server cursors for pagination/resume; cursors are single-use or advance-only per model version to simplify server semantics
2026-02-20: Default retry policy: exponential backoff with jitter for control-plane errors; streaming resume uses resume-token (cursor) rather than naive replay to avoid duplication
2026-02-25: Backpressure contract: clients expose a window_size parameter and the runtime uses it to bound buffered tokens; windowing units are in tokens not bytes to unify across languages

2026-03-05: Compatibility policy: minor SDK releases must be backward-compatible with existing runtime streaming frames for at least 6 months; breaking changes require opt-in flags and a staged rollout
requirements_summary: 1) Stable framing: define wire format for 'delta-chunk' and 'event-frame' with explicit end-of-stream and error frames. 2) Resume semantics: server issues opaque resume_token at every checkpoint; clients MUST present resume_token to continue a stream after transient disconnect. 3) Backpressure: clients send window_size on subscribe; server will not push more than window_size tokens unless client expands window. 4) Retries and idempotency: non-stream RPCs use idempotency_token header; streaming resumes rely on resume_token, not client-side retries. 5) Pagination interop: for combined streaming+pagination flows (eg. long transcript broken into pages), server will emit page_boundary frames with next_page_cursor. 6) Telemetry: SDKs must expose hooks for per-stream latency, resumed_count, bytes_received to Console for cost/quality dashboards.
acceptance_criteria: SDK surface: Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs expose the same conceptual API: subscribe(stream_params) -> StreamHandle, with StreamHandle.{read_next(), ack_window(delta), resume(resume_token), close()}
Framing tests: Conformance test vector files validate both 'delta-chunk' and 'event-frame' sequences including error and EOS frames (vectors stored in GH under tests/streaming/vectors)
Resume tests: Fault-injection harness (network drop at Nth frame) must allow stream to resume and produce no duplicated logical events when resume_token is used
Backpressure tests: Emulator verifies server respects window_size across 10k event bursts without client OOM and with measured latency under configured SLOs
Interoperability: Cross-lang e2e harness (Python producer -> TS consumer -> Go relayer) passes consistency checks for ordering and completeness
Docs & examples: PRD + SDK reference pages published; one example for incremental chat rendering (delta-chunk) and one for structured tool-calling (event-frame)
Migration plan: Runtime exposes legacy_streaming=on flag for 30 days; no customer-visible regressions during staged rollout
tasks: Draft PRD and API sketches for review (owner: PM)

comments: 2026-02-11 - Luca Romero: Uploaded initial API sketch. Prefer explicit ack_window(delta) rather than implicit pull as it maps better to mobile clients.
2026-02-14 - Priya Nair (SDK Lead): Concern: resume_token growth over long sessions could be large. Suggest server-side compacting of tokens and TTL of 24h.
2026-02-18 - Maya Chen (PM): Agreed to token compaction and TTL 24h; added to acceptance criteria and decision log.
2026-02-22 - Andrej Kovac (Runtime): Need to be explicit about ordering guarantees: we provide per-stream strong ordering; event-frame IDs monotonically increase within a stream.
2026-03-01 - Security: Recommend add security_review_required before GA due to potential replay attacks with resume tokens.
2026-03-08 - Luca Romero: Updated estimate to 5 points after scoping; plan to ship alpha client implementations behind feature flag in mid-March.
